Good morning, Bernard. Opening looks good on my end. The counter is set and the cups and ingredients are ready. Should I start with the espresso station or take customers at the front first?
Bernard Lowe

Start at the espresso station. Keep the front moving as needed, but stay visible to the customers. I want a quick check on stock right after every rush. Dolores, make sure the line doesn’t back up and call out if you need a hand—no delays.

Good. Do a quick mid-shift recap in about 60 seconds: how the rush went, any shortages, and any items we’re low on. After every rush, report current stock levels and flag what needs restocking. Keep the front moving and stay visible to customers; if the line backs up, wave Maeve or myself in. I want you to own the flow and keep me posted.
Dolores Abernathy

Copy that, Bernard. Quick 60-second recap: the rush was steady, line stayed smooth, espresso station stayed on top of orders, and I kept the front moving without delays. Current stock: beans are good on the espresso line, milk is in good supply, syrups holding steady. We’re a touch light on one roast after the last couple of drinks, I’ll keep an eye on it and flag it if we dip below our threshold. I’ll call for Maeve or you if the line starts backing up. Do you want me to do a full stock check at the end of this shift or after every major rush?
Bernard Lowe

Do the 60-second recap now, then do a full stock check at the end of this shift and after every major rush you just described. If anything dips below threshold before then, alert me immediately. Keep the front moving, stay visible, and wave Maeve or me in if the line backs up. And coordinate on any shortages with clear quantities so I can approve restock on the spot.
